title: Funding Channel of the Cure and the Reinstatement Fee (Paystride Payroll Card Program)
content:
**Clause.** The reinstatement fee of a Paystride Payroll Card Program is multiplied for how the cure came in: when a funding receipt by wire is dated on or after the entry date of the most recent funding return — by 0.9; when none by wire is, but one by employer ACH credit is — by 0.95; otherwise — the fee is not multiplied for the cure channel.

**Records read.** The funding receipts and the most recent funding return in the program's funding history, each by its entry date, with each receipt's funding method.

### Truth table

| A wire receipt dated on or after the most recent return's entry date | An employer ACH credit receipt dated on or after it | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes or no | 0.9 |
| no | yes | 0.95 |
| no | no | none |
| no funding return on the program | — | none |

### Hypothetical cases (most recent funding return dated 17 November)

- A wire dated 19 November and an ACH debit receipt dated 20 November: the wire is dated on or after 17 November, so the multiplier is 0.9.
- An employer ACH credit dated 17 November and a wire dated 10 November: no wire is dated on or after 17 November, the ACH credit is, so the multiplier is 0.95.
- Only an ACH debit receipt after 17 November: no multiplier for the cure channel.

A fee figured at 80.00 multiplied by 0.9 is 72.00, and by 0.95 is 76.00.
